What constitutes task complexity for agents in real-world applications?
The agent interacts with both databases (through API tools) and a simulated user.

We construct 66 tools across three domains—delivery, in-store consumption, and online travel services—and model their intrinsic dependencies as a graph structure where policy information is inherently encoded.

We model inter-tool dependencies as a directed graph G = (V, E) and augment tool descriptions with pre-conditions (states required before execution) and post-conditions (expected outcomes after execution).

In this paper, we introduce VitaBench, a challenging benchmark that evaluates agents on versatile interactive tasks grounded in real-world settings.

Through a framework that eliminates domain-specific policies, we enable flexible composition of these scenarios and tools, yielding 100 cross-scenario tasks (main results) and 300 single-scenario tasks.
VitaBench presents agents with the most complex life-serving simulation environment to date, comprising 66 tools.
Our comprehensive evaluation reveals that even the most advanced models achieve only 32.5% success rate on cross-scenario tasks, and less than 62% success rate on others.
The name “Vita” derives from the Latin word for “Life”, reflecting our focus on life-serving applications.
VitaBench provides an evaluation framework that supports model evaluations on both single-domain and cross-domain tasks through flexible configuration.
For cross-domain evaluation, simply connect multiple domain names with commas
